problem: National expense fitting can leak heldout-region representation information.
effect: A region-outcome-only split cannot establish full-pipeline generalization.
check: All 72 new folds exclude heldout expenses from scaler, annual training profiles, K4/H75 initialization and fitting. All 144 saved rules/labels and 72 H75 training guards independently reconstructed; fixed prediction arithmetic verified.
limitation: Historical architecture selection used national 2023 expenses; the new fold fitting is strict, architecture-selection independence is not claimed.

problem: Evaluation-batch centering or future fitting can change nominal inductive predictions.
effect: Batch composition and future data can alter the fitted rule or its provenance.
check: Future perturbation, row/chunk/order/batch isolation, pre-median correction, unknown identities and missing calendar support tested. Exact consumed-byte readers and exclusive CLI writes verified.
limitation: Fixed-reference R requires current reference data and is a separately scoped contextual view.

problem: Calendar/reliability arms could be promoted using their own transformed metric alone.
effect: Apparent fitted-space improvement can hide common-space/occupancy loss.
check: All three fixed arms fail the declared joint screen; baseline remains. Export guards preserve all 12,096 archived labels.
scope: Candidate promotion only; implementation and reproducibility checks pass.

problem: A difference of population medians need not equal the median of paired changes.
effect: Population-composition changes can be mistaken for reference-entity changes.
check: Fixed IDs paired before monthly median; all 12 packets and 2,016 A/R labels independently reconstructed. Missing-reference order-statistic intervals and 384 synthetic box vertices checked; 11 historical missing controls contain the known full median.
limitation: ARI 0.722494/218 changes is descriptive. Exact geometric certificates at epsilon=0 assume their declared boxes; no support, causal, boundary-continuity or future guarantees. Territorial transitions remain unresolved.

problem: A family-specific H75 wage result may be presented as universal economic superiority.
effect: Probe-family dependence and a stronger continuous comparator can be obscured.
check: 24 scores and 288 fixed-prediction bootstrap comparisons independently recomputed. H75 beats K4 with positive conditional intervals only for histogram probes; linear/quadratic intervals cross zero. Continuous-five histogram has lower observed RMSE in both years.
limitation: Intervals are conditional on fixed overlapping-fold predictions and do not include architecture selection or multiplicity correction.

problem: 2024 outcome scoring may be mistaken for an untouched future confirmation.
effect: Outcome timing and retrospective cohort selection can overstate deployment evidence.
check: The same 2023-fitted predictions, controls and representation score 1,678 entities/68 regions in 2024, versus 1,797/72 in 2023; no 2024 fit or covariates. Centered error variance remains an after-prediction diagnostic.
limitation: Exploratory retrospective 2023-to-2024 backtest with previously inspected outcomes; no prospective guarantee.

problem: Sector eligibility could accidentally inherit wage observability.
effect: The target cohort and missingness interpretation would be biased.
check: All 2,016 registry rows start the join; population independently reconstructed from its own verified total series. There are 1,797 positive, one zero and 218 missing population values; the 1,797 positive cases empirically also have wages. Sector eligibility uses controls, not wage availability.
limitation: The sector estimand is conditional on valid controls for 1,797 entities/72 regions, not all 2,016 expense entities.

problem: Observed-case sector scores discard missing targets and entire missing regions.
effect: A complete-case advantage need not hold for the fixed eligible cohort.
check: 864 probes and 48 bound comparisons reconstructed from fixed predictions; missing-region denominators retained. All 36 nonself equal-region bounds cross zero.
limitation: No arbitrary-missingness advantage established for these three sector targets. Bounds are finite-cohort identification bounds over [0,1], not confidence intervals; no joint sector constraints imposed.

problem: Official MQ definition and final reviewer access are unavailable in local code evidence.
effect: A complete six-ICVI or submission-access claim cannot be certified.
check: Current official page names MQ without a formula/reference. Repository existence is separate from jury view access; no access or privacy changes performed.
limitation: External definition/access gaps are separate from passed implementation gates.
